name: One-tape palindrome lower bound
statement: For Σ = {0,1,#}, the palindrome language PAL = {z ∈ Σ* : z = rev(z)} requires Ω(n²) time on every one-tape Turing machine.

name: Crossing-sequence disjointness
statement: For distinct x,y ∈ PALₙ, the sets C(x) and C(y) of crossing sequences in the middle half of the input are disjoint.

name: Sub-log-log space collapse
statement: Every Turing machine using o(log log n) work space accepts a regular language. This is tight up to constants: a specific nonregular language is accepted in O(log log n) space.

name: Constant accepted-space bound
statement: If a machine uses at most a fixed finite number of work-tape cells on every accepted input, then its accepted language is regular.

name: Time- and space-bounded machines
statement: A nondeterministic TM is T(n)-time-bounded when, except on finitely many inputs, every computation path halts within T(|x|) steps. It is S(n)-space-bounded when, except on finitely many inputs, every path uses at most S(|x|) work-tape cells.

name: Basic time and space classes
statement: DTIME(T), NTIME(T), DSPACE(S), and NSPACE(S) are the languages accepted within the indicated deterministic or nondeterministic time or space bound. For a class A, co-A is the class of complements of languages in A.

name: Linear speedup
statement: For T(n) ≥ n+1, S(n) = Ω(log n), and every constant c ≥ 1: DTIME(cT) ⊆ DTIME(T), NTIME(cT) ⊆ NTIME(T), DSPACE(cS) ⊆ DSPACE(S), and NSPACE(cS) ⊆ NSPACE(S).

name: Named complexity classes
statement: LOGSPACE = DSPACE(log n), NLOGSPACE = NSPACE(log n), P = ⋃ₖ DTIME(nᵏ), NP = ⋃ₖ NTIME(nᵏ), PSPACE = ⋃ₖ DSPACE(nᵏ), NPSPACE = ⋃ₖ NSPACE(nᵏ), and analogously EXPTIME, NEXPTIME, EXPSPACE, and NEXPSPACE use bounds 2^{nᵏ}.

name: Basic time-space inclusions
statement: For S(n) ≥ log n: DTIME(T) ⊆ DSPACE(T), NTIME(T) ⊆ NSPACE(T), DSPACE(S) ⊆ DTIME(2^{O(S)}), and NSPACE(S) ⊆ NTIME(2^{O(S)}).

name: Deterministic simulation bounds
statement: For S(n) ≥ log n: NTIME(T) ⊆ DSPACE(T), and NSPACE(S) ⊆ DTIME(2^{O(S)}).

name: Savitch’s theorem
statement: For S(n) ≥ log n, NSPACE(S(n)) ⊆ DSPACE(S(n)²). In particular, PSPACE = NPSPACE.
significance: Converts nondeterministic space into only a quadratic deterministic-space overhead.

name: Deterministic space hierarchy
statement: If S is space-constructible, then DSPACE(S) contains a language outside DSPACE(S′) for every S′ = o(S).

name: Deterministic time hierarchy
statement: If T is time-constructible and T(n) ≥ n, then DTIME(T) contains a language outside every DTIME(T′) satisfying T′(n) log T′(n) = o(T(n)).

name: Immerman–Szelepcsényi theorem
statement: For every S(n) ≥ log n, NSPACE(S(n)) is closed under complement: NSPACE(S(n)) = co-NSPACE(S(n)).
significance: Shows nondeterministic space is closed under complement, including NL = coNL.

name: Transitivity of logspace reductions
statement: Logspace many-one reducibility is transitive: if A ≤ₘˡᵒᵍ B and B ≤ₘˡᵒᵍ C, then A ≤ₘˡᵒᵍ C.

name: LOGSPACE as reduction to a fixed language
statement: A language A is in LOGSPACE exactly when A ≤ₘˡᵒᵍ {0,1}.

name: Closure under logspace reduction
statement: If A ≤ₘˡᵒᵍ B and B ∈ LOGSPACE, then A ∈ LOGSPACE.

name: Logspace reductions are polynomial-time reductions
statement: If A ≤ₘˡᵒᵍ B, then A ≤ₘᵖ B.

name: MAZE / directed reachability
statement: MAZE asks whether a directed graph G with distinguished vertices s and t contains a directed path from s to t.

name: NLOGSPACE-completeness of reachability
statement: MAZE is complete for NLOGSPACE under logspace many-one reductions.

name: Reachability criterion for L = NL
statement: MAZE is in LOGSPACE if and only if LOGSPACE = NLOGSPACE.

name: P-completeness of circuit value
statement: The Boolean circuit value problem is complete for P under logspace many-one reductions.

name: Cook–Levin theorem, logspace form
statement: Boolean satisfiability is complete for NP under logspace many-one reductions.
significance: Provides the canonical complete problem for NP.

label: A.3
name: Infima of prefixpoints
statement: The infimum of any family of prefixpoints of a monotone operator is again a prefixpoint.

label: A.4
name: Least fixpoint existence
statement: Every monotone operator on a complete lattice has a least fixpoint.

label: A.5
name: Prefixpoint closure operator
statement: For a monotone operator τ, the map τ†(x), defined as the least prefixpoint of τ above x, is a closure operator.

label: A.8
name: Monotonicity of transfinite approximants
statement: For ordinals α ≤ β, the transfinite iterates satisfy τ^α(x) ≤ τ^β(x).

label: A.9
name: Knaster–Tarski theorem
statement: For every monotone operator τ on a complete lattice, the least prefixpoint above x equals the supremum of the transfinite iteration from below: τ†(x) = τ*(x).
significance: Supplies the fixed-point machinery used for alternating computation and games.

name: Alternating Turing machine
statement: An alternating Turing machine is a nondeterministic TM whose states are typed as AND, OR, or NOT states; NOT configurations have exactly one successor. An accepting leaf is an AND state with no successors, and a rejecting leaf is an OR state with no successors.

name: Acceptance for alternating machines
statement: Let ℓ* be the least fixed-point labeling of configurations by {0,1,⊥}. The machine accepts x when ℓ*(start(x)) = 1 and rejects x when ℓ*(start(x)) = 0; value ⊥ means neither acceptance nor rejection.

name: Eliminating negation states
statement: Every alternating TM with NOT states can be simulated by an alternating TM using only AND and OR states, with no asymptotic increase in time or space.

name: Alternation simulation theorem
statement: For T(n) ≥ n and S(n) ≥ log n: (i) ATIME(T) ⊆ DSPACE(T); (ii) DSPACE(S) ⊆ ATIME(S²); (iii) ASPACE(S) ⊆ DTIME(2^{O(S)}); and (iv) DTIME(T) ⊆ ASPACE(log T).
significance: Identifies alternation as the bridge between time and space.

name: Alternation characterizations
statement: For T(n) ≥ n and S(n) ≥ log n, ATIME(T^{O(1)}) = DSPACE(T^{O(1)}) and ASPACE(S) = DTIME(2^{O(S)}).

name: Quantified Boolean formula problem
statement: QBF asks whether a fully quantified Boolean expression Q₁x₁…Qₙxₙ B(x₁,…,xₙ), with each Qᵢ ∈ {∃,∀}, is true over {0,1}.

name: PSPACE-completeness of QBF
statement: QBF is complete for PSPACE under logspace many-one reductions.

name: Forced-win predicate
statement: For a two-player perfect-information game, checkmate(y) means y has no legal successor. The predicate win is the least fixed point satisfying win(x) iff there exists a move x→y such that every legal reply y→z leads to win(z) (with immediate checkmate covered vacuously).

name: PSPACE-completeness of generalized geography
statement: Generalized geography is complete for PSPACE under logspace many-one reductions.

name: Bounded-alternation machines
statement: A Σₖ-machine is an alternating TM whose paths have at most k maximal blocks of like-typed configurations and begin with an OR block. A Πₖ-machine is defined dually and begins with an AND block; Σ₁ is nondeterminism and Σ₀ = Π₀ is determinism.

name: Levels of the polynomial hierarchy
statement: Σₖᵖ is the class accepted in polynomial time by Σₖ-machines, and Πₖᵖ is the class accepted in polynomial time by Πₖ-machines. Thus Σ₁ᵖ = NP, Π₁ᵖ = coNP, and Σ₀ᵖ = Π₀ᵖ = P.

name: Basic polynomial-hierarchy relations
statement: For every k: Πₖᵖ = co-Σₖᵖ; Σₖᵖ ∪ Πₖᵖ ⊆ Σₖ₊₁ᵖ ∩ Πₖ₊₁ᵖ; and ⋃ₖΣₖᵖ = ⋃ₖΠₖᵖ ⊆ PSPACE.

name: Generic Σₖᵖ-complete problem
statement: The bounded alternating acceptance language Hₖ is complete for Σₖᵖ under logspace many-one reductions.

name: Generic Πₖᵖ-complete problem
statement: The complement of Hₖ is complete for Πₖᵖ under logspace many-one reductions.

name: Relativized polynomial classes
statement: For an oracle B, Pᴮ and NPᴮ are the languages accepted by polynomial-time deterministic and nondeterministic oracle machines using B. For a class C, Pᶜ = ⋃_{B∈C}Pᴮ and NPᶜ = ⋃_{B∈C}NPᴮ.

name: Polynomial-time Turing reduction
statement: A ≤ᵀᵖ B means A ∈ Pᴮ; this is polynomial-time Turing (Cook) reducibility.

name: Oracle definition of PH
statement: Define NP₁ = NP and NPₖ₊₁ = NP^{NPₖ}. Then NPₖ = Σₖᵖ for every k ≥ 1.

name: Equivalence of PH definitions
statement: For every k ≥ 1, the iterated-oracle class NPₖ equals the alternating-machine class Σₖᵖ.

name: Quantifier characterization of Σₖᵖ
statement: A language A is in Σₖᵖ iff there are a polynomial-time predicate R and constant c such that x ∈ A exactly when ∃y₁∀y₂∃y₃…Qₖyₖ R(x,y₁,…,yₖ), where every |yᵢ| ≤ |x|ᶜ and Qₖ is ∃ for odd k and ∀ for even k.

name: Uniform-circuit definition of NC
statement: A logspace-uniform circuit family has n-input circuits Cₙ of polynomial size and polylogarithmic depth, constructible from 0ⁿ by a logspace transducer. NC is the class of languages decided by such Boolean circuit families.

name: STA classes
statement: STA(S,T,A) consists of languages accepted by alternating TMs simultaneously bounded by space S(n), time T(n), and A(n) alternations. An asterisk means no bound; Σ or Π may specify the initial branch type.

name: Ruzzo’s characterization of NC
statement: NC = STA(log n, *, (log n)^{O(1)}).

name: Ruzzo’s characterization of NC
statement: NC = STA(log n, *, (log n)^{O(1)}).

name: RP and BPP
statement: A language is in RP if a polynomial-time randomized TM accepts yes-instances with probability at least 3/4 and never accepts no-instances. It is in BPP if the same machine errs with probability at most 1/4 on every input.

name: Schwartz–Zippel lemma
statement: If p is a nonzero n-variate polynomial of total degree d over a field F and S ⊆ F, then p has at most d|S|^{n-1} zeros in Sⁿ.

name: Random evaluation bound
statement: Under the hypotheses of Schwartz–Zippel, a uniformly random s ∈ Sⁿ satisfies p(s)=0 with probability at most d/|S|.

name: Amplification lemma
statement: For every polynomial nᵈ, an RP algorithm can be amplified so that yes-instances are accepted with probability at least 1−2^{-nᵈ} while no-instances are never accepted. A BPP algorithm can be amplified so that its error is at most 2^{-nᵈ}.

name: XOR-shift covering claim
statement: In the amplified BPP setup, let m be the number of random bits and Aₓ = {y : M(x,y) accepts}. Then x ∈ A iff there exist m shifts z₁,…,zₘ ∈ {0,1}ᵐ such that ⋃ⱼ(Aₓ ⊕ zⱼ) = {0,1}ᵐ.

label: B.1
name: Chinese remainder theorem
statement: For pairwise coprime positive integers n₁,…,nₖ and n = ∏ᵢnᵢ, the map x mod n ↦ (x mod n₁,…,x mod nₖ) is a ring isomorphism Zₙ ≅ Z_{n₁}×…×Z_{nₖ}.

label: B.2
name: Chinese remainder theorem for ideals
statement: If I₁,…,Iₖ are pairwise comaximal ideals of a commutative ring R and I = ⋂ᵢIᵢ, then R/I ≅ R/I₁×…×R/Iₖ via [x]_I ↦ ([x]_{I₁},…,[x]_{Iₖ}).

label: C.1
name: Fermat’s theorem / primitive root criterion
statement: An integer p ≥ 2 is prime iff some element of {1,…,p−1} has multiplicative order p−1 modulo p.

label: C.2
name: Euler totient divisor identity
statement: For every positive integer n, ∑_{m|n} φ(m) = n.

label: C.3
name: Degree of the order polynomial
statement: For k dividing q−1, the polynomial Φₖ whose roots are the elements of GF(q)* of order k has degree φ(k).

label: C.4
name: Pratt’s primality theorem
statement: The language PRIMES belongs to NP ∩ coNP.

name: Interactive proof system
statement: A protocol (P,V) is an interactive proof for A when V is probabilistic polynomial time, yes-instances are accepted with probability at least 3/4 with the honest prover, and no-instances are accepted with probability at most 1/4 against every prover strategy. IP is the class of languages with such protocols.

name: Simple quantified Boolean formula
statement: A QBF is simple when negations apply only to variables and, between any free occurrence of a variable in a quantified subformula and its binding quantifier, there is at most one intervening universal quantifier.

name: Simplifying QBFs
statement: Every quantified Boolean formula can be transformed in logspace into an equivalent simple formula with at most quadratic growth in size.

name: Low-degree arithmetization
statement: If ∑_{x∈{0,1}}D(x) or ∏_{x∈{0,1}}D(x) arises by arithmetizing a simple Boolean formula, then D(x) is equivalent modulo p to a polynomial over Zₚ whose degree is linear in the expression size.

name: Univariate root bound
statement: A nonzero polynomial d(x) ∈ Zₚ[x] of degree at most n vanishes at a uniformly random element of Zₚ with probability at most n/p.

name: PCP theorem
statement: NP = PCP(log n, 1): every NP language has a verifier using O(log n) random bits and O(1) proof queries, with perfect completeness and constant soundness.
significance: Foundation of modern hardness of approximation.

name: 7/8 approximation for MAX-3SAT
statement: There is a polynomial-time algorithm that, for a 3CNF formula with m clauses and three distinct variables per clause, finds an assignment satisfying at least 7m/8 clauses.

name: Hardness of approximating MAX-CLIQUE
statement: A polynomial-time constant-factor approximation algorithm for MAX-CLIQUE exists for some fixed α>0 iff P = NP.

name: Hardness of a PTAS for MAX-3SAT
statement: MAX-3SAT has a polynomial-time approximation scheme iff P = NP.

name: Linearity testing lemma
statement: Let F=Zₚ and V be finite-dimensional. If ε<1/6 and Pr_{u,v}[f(u+v)=f(u)+f(v)]>1−ε, then there is a linear g:V→F agreeing with f on at least a 1−3ε fraction of V.

name: Back-and-forth theorem for dense orders
statement: Any two countable dense linear orders without endpoints are isomorphic. More generally, every finite local isomorphism between such orders extends to a full isomorphism.

name: Complexity of dense linear order
statement: The first-order theory of dense linear orders without endpoints is PSPACE-complete.

name: Integer affine functions
statement: An integer affine function f:Rᵏ→R has the form c₀+∑ᵢcᵢxᵢ with integer coefficients. Its norm is ‖f‖ = max_{0≤i≤k}|cᵢ|; Aₘᵏ denotes those with norm at most m.

name: Bounded affine equivalence
statement: For a,b∈Rᵏ, define a ≡ₘᵏ b when every integer affine f with ‖f‖≤m has the same sign on a and b; equivalently, a and b satisfy the same bounded-coefficient linear inequalities.

name: One-step extension lemma
statement: If a ≡_{2m²}ᵏ b, then for every a′∈R there is b′∈R such that (a,a′) ≡ₘ^{k+1} (b,b′).

name: Finite representatives lemma
statement: If σ is the ≡_{2m²}ᵏ-class of a, then points of the form (a,f(a)/c), with f∈A_{2m²}ᵏ and |c|≤2m², include a representative of every ≡ₘ^{k+1}-class consistent with σ.

name: Logical invariance under bounded affine equivalence
statement: If a ≡_{r(n,ℓ)}ᵏ b, then a and b agree on every reduced formula with at most n quantifiers and integer constants of magnitude at most ℓ.

name: Upper bound for real addition
statement: The first-order theory Th(R,+,≤) belongs to STA(*,2^{O(n)},n).

name: Recursive decomposition of large integer ranges
statement: For Iₙ={z∈Z:0≤z<2^{2ⁿ}}, one has Iₙ₊₁ = {z₁z₂+z₃+z₄ : z₁,z₂,z₃,z₄∈Iₙ}.

name: S1S–automata correspondence
statement: (i) Every S1S formula φ(x,X) can be translated into a Muller automaton whose accepted track encodings are exactly the tuples satisfying φ. (ii) Every nondeterministic Büchi automaton over {0,1} can be translated into an S1S formula defining the sets whose characteristic strings it accepts.

name: König’s lemma
statement: Every infinite tree of finite branching degree has an infinite path.

name: Acceptance invariant in Safra’s construction
statement: The nondeterministic Büchi automaton B accepts x iff, in the determinized construction, some color’s bell rings infinitely often while that color’s buzzer sounds only finitely often.

name: Safra determinization theorem
statement: Every n-state nondeterministic Büchi automaton can be simulated by a deterministic Rabin automaton with at most 2^{O(n log n)} states and n Rabin pairs.

name: Oracle collapsing P and NP
statement: There exists a recursive oracle A such that Pᴬ = NPᴬ.

name: Oracle separating P and NP
statement: There exists a recursive oracle B such that Pᴮ ≠ NPᴮ.

name: Fortune’s sparse-hard-set theorem
statement: If a sparse language is polynomial-time many-one hard for coNP, then P = NP.

name: Mahaney’s theorem
statement: If a sparse language is polynomial-time many-one complete for NP, then P = NP.

label: F.1
name: Random subspace isolation lemma
statement: Let S be a nonempty subset of GF(2)ⁿ, and choose a random nested tower E₀⊂…⊂Eₙ with dim(Eᵢ)=i. Then Pr[there exists i with |S∩Eᵢ|=1] ≥ 3/4.

label: F.2
name: Valiant–Vazirani theorem
statement: NP ⊆ RP^USAT: every NP language has a randomized polynomial-time reduction to unique satisfiability.

label: G.1
name: Toda’s theorem
statement: PH ⊆ P^#P.
significance: Shows the entire polynomial hierarchy is controlled by a counting oracle.

label: G.2
name: Operator identities used in Toda’s theorem
statement: For every class C downward closed under polynomial-time Turing reductions: (i) Σᵖ·C ⊆ R·Σˡᵒᵍ·⊕·C; (ii) Πˡᵒᵍ·⊕·C ⊆ ⊕·C; (iii) ⊕·BP·C ⊆ BP·⊕·C; (iv) BP·BP·C ⊆ BP·C; (v) ⊕·⊕·C ⊆ ⊕·C; and (vi) BP·C and ⊕·C are downward closed under ≤ᵀᵖ.

name: Circuit lower bounds imply oracle separation
statement: If parity has no depth-d circuit family of size 2^{(log n)^c} for any constants c and d, then some oracle A satisfies PHᴬ ≠ PSPACEᴬ.

name: Many variables survive a random restriction
statement: Under the lecture’s random partial valuation, the probability that fewer than √n/2 variables remain unassigned is at most (2/e)^{√n/2}.

name: Few variables survive inside a small set
statement: For a constant c and a variable set A with c ≤ |A| and |A| = o(n^{1/c}), the probability that a random partial valuation leaves more than c variables of A unassigned is at most n^{1−c/2} for all sufficiently large n.

name: Hitting many disjoint small sets
statement: Let S contain at least b log n pairwise disjoint variable sets, each of size <a. If E(A) is the event that all variables in A are assigned 0, then for sufficiently large n the probability that no E(A) occurs is at most n^{b log(1−2^{-a})}.

name: Bounded bottom fan-in
statement: If parity has polynomial-size depth-d circuits, then it has polynomial-size depth-d t-circuits for some constant t.

name: Reduce bottom fan-in
statement: If parity has polynomial-size depth-d t-circuits with d≥3 and t≥1, then it has polynomial-size depth-d (t−1)-circuits.

name: Remove a circuit level
statement: If parity has polynomial-size depth-d 1-circuits, then it has polynomial-size circuits of depth d−1.

name: Parity is not shallow CNF/DNF
statement: No (n−1)-CNF and no (n−1)-DNF computes parity on n inputs.

name: Furst–Saxe–Sipser lower bound
statement: Parity is not in AC⁰.
significance: A foundational unconditional circuit lower bound.

label: H.1
name: Minterm restriction lemma
statement: Let M be a minterm of φ∧C. Assign the variables shared by M and clause C in the unique way that keeps M nonzero. Then the restricted formula φ∧C equals the restricted φ, and the restricted M is a minterm of the restricted φ.

label: H.2
name: Eliminating a variable set
statement: For φ^{-W}=∧_{τ:W→{0,1}}τ(φ): (i) if φ is CNF, φ^{-W} has an equivalent CNF with no more clauses; (ii) any minterm of φ disjoint from W remains a minterm of φ^{-W}; (iii) restrictions fixing no variable of W commute with −W; and (iv) under such restrictions, φ is true iff φ^{-W} is true.

label: H.3
name: Håstad switching lemma
statement: Let φ be a t-CNF. Independently set each variable to 0 or 1 with probability (1−p)/2 each, or leave it unset with probability p. Then Pr[the restricted φ is not equivalent to an s-DNF] ≤ αˢ, where α=4pt/ln 2≈5.77pt.

label: H.4
name: Strong constant-depth parity lower bound
statement: For no constants c,d does parity have a depth-d circuit family of size 2^{(log n)^c}.
significance: Strong enough to produce a relativized PH–PSPACE separation.

label: H.5
name: Oracle separation of PH and PSPACE
statement: There exists an oracle A such that PHᴬ ≠ PSPACEᴬ.

name: Gap theorem
statement: For every total recursive f with f(x)≥x, there is a time bound T such that DTIME(f∘T)=DTIME(T); hence the interval between T and f(T) contains no new deterministic time class.

name: Blum speedup theorem
statement: For every monotone total recursive f with f(n)≥n², there is a recursive language A such that every TM Mᵢ deciding A has another decider Mⱼ for A with f(Tⱼ(x))<Tᵢ(x) for almost all x.

name: Recursion theorem
statement: For every total recursive index transformation σ, there is an index i with φᵢ=φ_{σ(i)}; such an i is effectively computable from an index for σ.

name: No enumerable list of minimal indices
statement: In any Gödel numbering, there is no infinite recursively enumerable list consisting entirely of minimal indices.

name: Effective padding lemma
statement: In every Gödel numbering there is a total recursive σ such that σ(x)>x and φₓ=φ_{σ(x)} for all x.

name: Rogers isomorphism theorem
statement: For any two Gödel numberings (φᵢ) and (ψᵢ) of the partial recursive functions, there is a recursive bijection ρ of N such that φᵢ=ψ_{ρ(i)} for every i.

label: J.1
name: Abstract gap theorem
statement: For an abstract complexity measure Φ and every total recursive f(x)≥x, there is a total recursive t with C_t^Φ=C_{f∘t}^Φ. Equivalently, every program bounded by f(t(x)) almost everywhere has an equivalent program bounded by t(x) almost everywhere.

label: J.2
name: Abstract speedup theorem
statement: For every abstract complexity measure Φ and total recursive f, there is a total recursive function g such that every index i for g has another index j for g with f(n,Φⱼ(n))<Φᵢ(n) almost everywhere.

label: J.3
name: Union theorem
statement: For every recursively enumerable nondecreasing list f₀≤f₁≤… of total recursive bounds, there is a total recursive f such that C_f^Φ=⋃ᵢC_{fᵢ}^Φ.

name: Quantifier characterization of the arithmetic hierarchy
statement: A∈Σₙ⁰ iff A={x:∃y₁∀y₂∃y₃…Qₙyₙ R(x,y₁,…,yₙ)} for some decidable R, with Qₙ=∃ for odd n and ∀ for even n. Dually, A∈Πₙ⁰ iff the prefix begins universally and alternates.

name: Finite-halting completeness lift
statement: FINHP is many-one complete for Σ₃⁰. More generally, if A is many-one complete for Σₙ⁰, then FIN_A is many-one complete for Σ_{n+2}⁰.

name: Post’s theorem on intermediate m-degrees
statement: There exists a recursively enumerable, nonrecursive language that is not r.e.-complete.

name: Immune set
statement: A set A⊆N is immune when it is infinite but contains no infinite recursively enumerable subset.

name: Simple set
statement: A set B⊆N is simple when B is recursively enumerable and its complement is immune; equivalently, the complement is infinite and B meets every infinite r.e. set.

name: Productive set
statement: A set C⊆N is productive when there is a total recursive function σ such that Wₓ⊆C implies σ(x)∈C∖Wₓ. Such σ is a productive function.

name: Existence of a simple set
statement: There exists a simple set.

name: Simple complements are not productive
statement: If B is simple, then its complement is not productive.

name: Completeness implies productivity of the complement
statement: If A is r.e.-complete, then its complement is productive.

name: Friedberg–Muchnik theorem
statement: There exists an r.e. set A of intermediate Turing degree: ∅ <ᵀ A <ᵀ K.
significance: Solves Post’s problem by constructing an intermediate r.e. Turing degree.

name: Low set
statement: An r.e. set A is low when Kᴬ ≤ᵀ K; equivalently, the halting problem relative to A is no harder than the ordinary halting problem.

name: Low sets are incomplete
statement: If A is low, then A <ᵀ K.

name: Low simple set
statement: There exists a low simple set.

name: Kleene’s theorem
statement: Over the natural numbers, the inductive relations are exactly the Π₁¹ relations, and the hyperelementary relations are exactly the Δ₁¹ relations.
significance: Connects inductive definitions with the first analytic level.

name: Ordinal characterization of inductive sets
statement: A set A⊆N is inductive iff there is a hyperelementary relation R with A={x:∃α<ω₁^{CK} R(x,α)}; equivalently, the existential witness can be a code for a recursive ordinal.

name: Harel’s theorem
statement: There is a recursive bijective encoding τ from binary trees to nontrivial full ω-trees such that a binary tree is fairly terminating for the condition (true,last(0)) iff τ(T) is well-founded.

name: Complexity of fair termination
statement: Fair termination is Π₁¹-complete.
significance: Places a natural program-termination problem at Π₁¹-complete complexity.

name: Verifier definition of NP
statement: A language L is in NP iff there are a polynomial p and a polynomial-time verifier M such that x∈L exactly when some certificate u∈{0,1}^{p(|x|)} satisfies M(x,u)=1.

name: Basic inclusions
statement: P ⊆ NP ⊆ EXP.

name: Nondeterministic time
statement: L∈NTIME(T(n)) when some nondeterministic TM decides L in O(T(n)) time on every computation branch.

name: Machine characterization of NP
statement: NP = ⋃_{c∈N} NTIME(nᶜ).

name: Karp reduction, NP-hardness, NP-completeness
statement: L≤ᵖL′ when a polynomial-time function f maps x∈L exactly to f(x)∈L′. A language is NP-hard if every NP language reduces to it, and NP-complete if it is both NP-hard and in NP.

name: Consequences of polynomial reductions
statement: (1) Polynomial-time Karp reductions are transitive. (2) If an NP-hard language lies in P, then P=NP. (3) An NP-complete language lies in P iff P=NP.

name: NP-completeness of TMSAT
statement: TMSAT = {⟨α,x,1ⁿ,1ᵗ⟩ : some u∈{0,1}ⁿ makes machine Mα accept ⟨x,u⟩ within t steps} is NP-complete.

name: Cook–Levin theorem
statement: SAT is NP-complete, and 3SAT is NP-complete.
significance: The central theorem establishing natural NP-complete problems.

name: NP-hardness of SAT
statement: SAT is NP-hard.

name: Universality of AND, OR, NOT
statement: Every Boolean function f:{0,1}^ℓ→{0,1} has an ℓ-variable CNF formula of size at most ℓ·2^ℓ that computes f.

name: Reduction from SAT to 3SAT
statement: SAT ≤ᵖ 3SAT.

name: NP-completeness of independent set
statement: INDSET is NP-complete.

name: NP-completeness of 0/1 integer programming
statement: 0/1 IPROG is NP-complete.

name: NP-completeness of directed Hamiltonian path
statement: The directed Hamiltonian path language dHAMPATH is NP-complete.

name: Decision-to-search under P=NP
statement: If P=NP, then for every NP language and every polynomial-time verifier, a valid certificate for any yes-instance can be found in polynomial time.
significance: Shows that, for NP problems, efficient decision would yield efficient witness recovery.

name: coNP by complementation
statement: coNP = {L : the complement of L is in NP}.

name: Universal-certificate characterization of coNP
statement: A language L is in coNP iff there are a polynomial p and polynomial-time M such that x∈L exactly when M(x,u)=1 for every u∈{0,1}^{p(|x|)}.

name: Padding implication
statement: If EXP ≠ NEXP, then P ≠ NP.

name: Deterministic one-tape Turing machine
statement: A finite-control machine with a semi-infinite read/write tape, a head, input and tape alphabets, and a transition function δ:Q×Γ→Q×Γ×{L,R}; it accepts or rejects by entering distinguished halting states.

name: Nondeterministic Turing machine
statement: A Turing machine whose transition rule is a finite relation rather than a function. Its computation is a tree, and it accepts when some branch reaches an accepting configuration.

name: Crossing sequence
statement: The sequence of finite-control states seen as a one-tape TM crosses a fixed boundary between adjacent tape cells. Crossing sequences transfer all information communicated across that boundary.

name: Logspace transducer
statement: A total deterministic logspace machine with read-only input, O(log n) read/write work space, and a write-only output tape. Its output defines a logspace-computable function.

name: Logspace many-one reduction
statement: A≤ₘˡᵒᵍB when a logspace-computable function σ satisfies x∈A iff σ(x)∈B. Hardness and completeness are defined using this reduction.

name: Complete lattice and monotone operator
statement: A complete lattice has a supremum for every subset. An operator τ is monotone when x≤y implies τ(x)≤τ(y); chain-continuity preserves suprema of chains, and finitary set operators depend only on finite subsets.

name: Prefixpoint, fixpoint, and closure operator
statement: A prefixpoint satisfies τ(x)≤x; a fixpoint satisfies τ(x)=x. A closure operator is monotone, extensive, and idempotent.

name: Alternating time and space classes
statement: ATIME(T) and ASPACE(S) are the languages accepted by alternating TMs whose every path respects the stated time or space bound.

name: Boolean circuit and circuit value problem
statement: A Boolean circuit is an acyclic network of Boolean gates. CVP supplies both a circuit and its input assignment and asks for the output value.

name: Oracle Turing machine
statement: An oracle machine may ask membership questions about a fixed set B and receive each answer in one step, enabling relativized classes such as Pᴮ and NPᴮ.

name: Probabilistic Turing machine
statement: A deterministic TM with access to a read-only random bit tape; acceptance probability is measured over uniformly random bit strings.

name: BPP lies low in PH
statement: BPP ⊆ Σ₂ᵖ ∩ Π₂ᵖ. The proof amplifies the randomized algorithm and uses a small family of XOR shifts to cover the random-bit space.

name: PCP(r,q)
statement: PCP(r(n),q(n)) consists of languages with polynomial-time proof verifiers using O(r(n)) random bits and O(q(n)) oracle queries, with perfect completeness and constant soundness.

name: IP = PSPACE
statement: Every PSPACE language has an interactive proof, and every language with an interactive proof is in PSPACE; therefore IP = PSPACE.

name: Weak PCP construction
statement: NP ⊆ PCP(n³,1), proved using arithmetization, linearity testing, tensor-consistency tests, and random self-correction.

name: First-order structure, formula, sentence, and theory
statement: A structure interprets a signature over a domain; terms denote elements, formulas receive truth values under valuations, sentences have no free variables, and Th(A) is the set of sentences true in A.

name: Exact complexity of real addition
statement: The first-order theory Th(R,+,≤) is complete for STA(*,2^{O(n)},n).

name: Exact complexity of Presburger arithmetic
statement: The first-order theory Th(Z,+,≤) is complete for STA(*,2^{2^{n^{O(1)}}},n).

name: Büchi automaton
statement: An automaton on infinite words whose run is accepting when a designated accepting state occurs infinitely often.

name: Muller automaton
statement: An automaton on infinite words with an acceptance family F⊆2^Q; a run is accepting when its set of infinitely recurring states belongs to F.

name: Rabin automaton
statement: A deterministic ω-automaton with pairs (Gᵢ,Rᵢ); a run accepts when some Gᵢ is visited infinitely often while the corresponding Rᵢ is visited only finitely often.

name: Sparse language
statement: A language S is sparse when the number of strings of length at most n in S is bounded by a polynomial in n.

name: Unique satisfiability
statement: USAT is the promise-style satisfiability problem restricted to formulas having at most one satisfying assignment; it is used as the target of the Valiant–Vazirani randomized reduction.

name: The class #P
statement: #P consists of functions counting accepting computation paths of nondeterministic polynomial-time machines. P^#P denotes polynomial-time computation with access to such counts.

name: AC⁰
statement: AC⁰ is the class of constant-depth, polynomial-size Boolean circuit families with unbounded-fan-in AND and OR gates and negations at inputs.

name: Gödel numbering
statement: An effective enumeration φ₀,φ₁,… of the partial recursive functions supporting universal simulation and effective program manipulation.

name: Arithmetic hierarchy
statement: The classes Σₙ⁰ and Πₙ⁰ classify sets definable by n alternating first-order number quantifiers over a decidable predicate, beginning existentially or universally.

name: Many-one and Turing degrees
statement: A≤ₘB uses a total recursive many-one map; A≤ᵀB means A is decidable with oracle B. Mutual reducibility defines m-degrees and Turing degrees.

name: Analytic hierarchy
statement: The analytic hierarchy extends the arithmetic hierarchy by allowing second-order quantification over sets or functions; its first universal level Π₁¹ contains well-foundedness-type problems.

name: Fair termination
statement: A computation tree is fairly terminating when every fair path terminates; the lecture reduces this property to well-foundedness of recursively encoded ω-trees.

name: Certificate / witness
statement: A polynomial-length string u that causes a polynomial-time verifier M(x,u) to accept, thereby certifying that x is a yes-instance of an NP language.

name: Nondeterministic Turing machine
statement: A TM with multiple transition choices. It accepts an input when at least one sequence of nondeterministic choices reaches the accepting state.

name: CNF, SAT, and 3SAT
statement: A CNF formula is a conjunction of clauses, each a disjunction of literals. SAT asks whether a CNF formula is satisfiable; 3SAT restricts each clause to at most three literals.

name: Levin and parsimonious reductions
statement: A Levin reduction efficiently maps both instances and witnesses between NP problems. A parsimonious reduction additionally preserves the number of witnesses.

name: Downward self-reducibility
statement: SAT can recover a satisfying assignment by repeatedly fixing one variable and querying satisfiability of the smaller formulas; this converts a decision procedure into a search procedure.

name: EXP and NEXP
statement: EXP is deterministic exponential time ⋃₍c₎DTIME(2^{nᶜ}); NEXP is its nondeterministic analogue ⋃₍c₎NTIME(2^{nᶜ}).
